title: Identification of socioeconomic and psychosocial risk factors for poor glycemic control in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus, and development of a risk assessment score at the time of initial diagnosis
summary:
Type 1 diabetes is a chronic condition in which the body can no longer produce sufficient insulin. Good long-term blood glucose control is important to prevent acute complications and long-term health problems. However, even with modern diabetes treatment, there are considerable differences in blood glucose control between children and adolescents.

The aim of this study is to investigate which medical, psychological, treatment-related, and social characteristics are associated with better or poorer long-term blood glucose control. Existing medical records of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes treated at the pediatric diabetes center of University Hospital Halle are analyzed. The study examines long-term blood glucose values, acute metabolic complications, hospital admissions, the type of insulin treatment, the use of glucose sensors, psychiatric conditions, and selected family and regional characteristics.

No additional treatment or examination is performed as part of the study. The results may help to identify children and families with increased support needs at an earlier stage and to improve pediatric diabetes care.
conditions: Type 1 diabetes mellitus: without complications, not designated as uncontrolled

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus

Pediatric patients receiving diabetes care at the Department of Pediatrics I or II, University Hospital Halle (Saale), Germany

Treatment during the defined study period

At least three documented HbA1c measurements after onset of type 1 diabetes

Availability of sufficient routinely collected clinical data for retrospective analysis
Exclusion criteria:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus

Monogenic or other specific forms of diabetes, including MODY

Insufficient clinical documentation for analysis

Fewer than three documented HbA1c measurements after diabetes onset

Severe underlying conditions associated with substantial cognitive impairment where comparability with the remaining study population was not considered adequate
